uncurated_metadata: Study subjects: 35 Swedish health care students (23-34 years old, 74% female); Travel destinations: Indian peninsula (n=18) and Central Africa (n=17); Median travel duration: 34 days (range 14-150); Fecal specimens collected median 4 days before departure and 22 days after return; 69% subjects experienced traveler's diarrhea (median 4 days); All travelers excluded if antibiotics taken within 6 months prior to sampling; Metagenomic sequencing: Illumina HiSeq 2000; 70 libraries (57.7 to 463.8 million read pairs); 178 different resistance gene types detected; 23 found in all libraries, 35 in ≥90%; Nine resistance genes showed significant changes in abundance; ESBL genes detected in all subjects acquiring ESBL-positive E. coli on metagenomes; CTX-M-15 gene found in all ESBL-positive E. coli isolates from India group; No ESBL-positive isolates recovered from Central Africa group post-travel; Colocalization of resistance genes with mobile elements (integrases, ISCR elements); No significant correlation between resistance gene changes and traveler's diarrhea
